item.title: Man Utd's Yoro has Anfield red card overturned
item.description: Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak [Getty Images] Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card he was shown during Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool overturned. The Football Association has confirmed Yoro will now be clear to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday. "Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," said the FA in a statement. New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which came just eight minutes in and, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0. Liverpool striker Alexander Isak ran on to a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought the Swede down. Nevertheless, referee Sam Barrott sent Yoro off, drawing criticism from Pochettino. "The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down. "But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul." 'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves? Sporting boss Fonseca dismisses Man Utd fragile talk United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT). The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break. But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile". "I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon. "Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma. "Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day." United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions. Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect. "Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said. "I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict." item.title: 'I could throw three interceptions... and not want to go hang myself': Troy Aikman remembers Tom Jackson, 'NFL Primetime'
item.description: Credit: 'Monday Night Countdown' Troy Aikman’s tribute to Tom Jackson on Monday night was warm, heartfelt, and about one word choice away from going off without a hitch. Aikman appeared on Monday Night Countdown ahead of Bengals-Commanders to eulogize Jackson, who died Friday at 75 , and dedicated most of his remembrance to the sacrosanct Sunday night ritual that bookended nearly every week of his Hall of Fame career in Dallas. The 60-year-old Aikman recalled that arriving home after a game and tuning in to NFL Primetime was the only way a player of his generation could take stock of everything that had unfolded across the league. And for a quarterback, the show was also the definitive barometer of how his afternoon compared with the rival passers he was constantly measuring himself against. “Him and Boomer, they were so good, you know, obviously great friends, great chemistry, but what I respected probably as much as anything about that show was they could be critical and opinionated, but they didn’t attack people,” Aikman said. “Like I could throw three interceptions in a game and we could lose and I could watch Primetime and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They just had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened, but doing it the right way, I thought. And anyone who knew Tom knew that’s who he was.” Troy Aikman: “I could throw three interceptions in a game, and we could lose, and I could watch [NFL Primetime] and not want to go hang myself at the end of the night. They had a respectful way of presenting the information and letting everybody know what happened…” https://t.co/Fu3f0aiMpp — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 24, 2026 Beneath the clumsy wording, though, lay a sentiment that would resonate with anyone who spent Sunday nights in the late ’80s and ’90s waiting for Berman and Jackson to make sense of the afternoon. Primetime aired on Sunday nights from 1987 through 2005, a span that covered all 12 of Aikman’s seasons with the Cowboys; for most of that stretch, there was no RedZone, no streaming, and no highlight clipped and circulated online before the extra point sailed through the uprights. Berman supplied the nicknames and the bombast while Jackson, a 14-year Broncos linebacker who anchored the vaunted “Orange Crush” defense, gave viewers an authoritative account from a former player’s perspective. The show kept its stranglehold on Sunday nights until NBC locked up the extended highlight rights that came with Sunday Night Football . Berman broke the news himself on Sunday morning, opening Sunday NFL Countdown with an emotional tribute to the partner ESPN had once immortalized by naming its NFL studio after both men , and the program revived the beloved Jacked Up segment in Jackson’s memory. The timing made the loss all the more devastating. Only three weeks earlier, Jackson had surprised Berman at the Countdown studio during a visit filmed for an upcoming doc

item.description: Credit: Kirby Lee-USA TODAY Sports The Tennessee Titans still control the No. 1 spot in the 2027 NFL Draft despite a 51-30 loss to the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The franchise fell to 1-9 on the season, but they kept the top pick because of their weaker schedule compared to the other bad teams. The Los Angeles Chargers and Miami Dolphins also dropped to 1-9 records after their own losses, creating a three-way tie at the bottom of the league standings. According to a report , the Titans overtook the Chargers for the top spot last week after Los Angeles finally won a game, but the Chargers lost again on Sunday to the New York Jets. Now the race for the first overall selection is down to just these three clubs, and the tiebreaker rules will decide who gets the prize. Tiebreakers Favor Tennessee and Los Angeles Miami sits at third place in this race because the Dolphins face the toughest schedule of the three teams. According to reports, the Dolphins’ opponents have a .595 winning percentage, which is higher than the Titans’ .483 and the Chargers’ .531. This math means Miami needs to lose more games than the other two teams just to climb above them in the draft order. The Dolphins lost 26-9 to the Buffalo Bills on Sunday, marking their fourth straight defeat in a row. The team has been outscored 93-59 during this losing skid, and the offense has averaged under 15 points a game. Kyle Crabbs, who covers the Dolphins for Yahoo Sports, noted that the front office is not panicking despite the 1-8 start because everyone knew the roster was in a tough spot. The Quarterback Question Looms Large With the offense struggling, the need for a new quarterback has become the main topic for the Miami front office. Crabbs admitted he does not love any of the current quarterback prospects in the 2027 class. “I have a hard time falling in love with any of these guys,” Crabbs said. He listed Oklahoma State’s Drew Mestemaker, Notre Dame’s CJ Carr, and Miami’s Darien Mensah as names in play, but he feels the raw production does not reflect how Malik Willis has actually played. Willis is under contract for two more seasons, which gives the team a bridge to develop a rookie without rushing him onto the field. A Week 16 Showdown Could Decide It All A matchup at Hard Rock Stadium in Week 16 between the Chargers and Dolphins could decide which squad ends up with the poorest record. Both clubs face huge draft ramifications from that matchup as they try to secure the top pick. Miami hosts the Jets this week on Sunday, Nov. 29, before a long road trip that includes stops in Denver and Green Bay. The Dolphins have seven games left in the regular season, and two matchups against the Jets and Chargers look very winnable for the home team. item.title: Senegal reinstated as Afcon 2025 winners by court ruling
item.description: Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title [Getty Images] Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport. The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January. The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them. Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas), sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October. In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) 2025 winners. A statement issued by Cas said the court considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority". "By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume." The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always champions of Africa". "The FSF welcomes this ruling with deep satisfaction," it later said in a statement. "This decision affirms, above all, the triumph of sporting fairness and reaffirms a fundamental principle: the true outcome of a match is determined exclusively on the field of play, under the protection of sports law." Meanwhile, Morocco's football federation (FRMF) expressed "surprise" at the ruling and added that it would "pursue all available legal avenues to challenge the decision". Caf is yet to comment but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling. The full grounds for the decision will be published by Cas in due course unless the parties request confidentiality. item.title: Hackensack-Teaneck Thanksgiving football game rescheduled due to storm
item.description: Another piece of North Jersey’s fading Thanksgiving football tradition is being pushed off the holiday this year, this time by the weather. The annual rivalry game between Hackensack and Teaneck, a Thanksgiving fixture dating to 1931, has been moved to Wednesday evening as a coastal storm threatens the region with heavy rain and strong winds. Kickoff is now scheduled for 6 p.m. at Teaneck High School. The change leaves one of North Jersey’s longest-running holiday rivalries without its traditional Thanksgiving morning setting. The other remaining Thanksgiving Day game, between Tenafly and Dumont, was also moved to Wednesday night because of the forecast. Story continues below photo gallery. The game was originally scheduled for Thanksgiving morning at 10:30 a.m. Kick-off will now be 6 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 25, at Teaneck High School. “This decision was made with the safety and well-being of our student-athletes, twirlers, marching band, cheerleading teams, families, and community members as our top priority,” the Teaneck School District wrote in a statement. “We appreciate the understanding and flexibility of our students, families, alumni, and community members as we make this adjustment.” Ed Klimek, Teaneck's athletic director, said the main reason behind the decision was to allow the band, flag twirlers and cheerleaders, who had been practicing for weeks, to be able to perform. "Two years ago we played in an absolute monsoon," he said. "We can play football in the rain, but they can't perform in the rain. When I proposed this to Hackensack and to the football teams, everyone was on board." The parade to the field before the game, with the two teams’ school bands, cheerleaders and flag twirlers marching, is canceled, Klimek said. The traditional Thanksgiving Day team between the neighboring communities is one of the last played in North Jersey on the holiday. Many high school football teams have done away with the tradition of playing on Thanksgiving over the years, because of difficulties with the schedule and concerns that it would interfere with teams’ preparations for playing in championship games. The other remaining game scheduled for Thanksgiving Day between Tenafly and Dumont was also rescheduled to 6 p.m. Wednesday and will be played at Geissinger Field in Tenafly. The annual Thanksgiving Day rivalry game between Hackensack Comets and Teaneck Highwaymen dates back to 1931. Teaneck’s record for the season is 7-3. Hackensack is 4-4. Hackensack has dominated the matchup in recent years and has won the past 12 meetings between the two. item.title: Chris Johnson responds to uncalled Josh Allen unsportsmanlike penalty
item.description: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen certainly could have been called for unsportsmanlike conduct in a recent defeat of the Miami Dolphins , but wasn't. Dolphins rookie cornerback Chris Johnson and Allen were pushing and shoving at the end of an interception return by Jacob Rodriguez . Johnson was blocking Allen near a sideline when Allen appeared to fling him to ground by a facemask. Allen then shoved Johnson again when they are out of bounds. Was it a simple football play? Or should it have been a 15-yard penalty? Johnson said: "I saw J-Rod get the pick and from there on, I'm looking for a block. It just happened to be Josh Allen. I guess he didn't appreciate it much. And then we got tied up a bit." Johnson said he was surprised no flag was thrown. "Once you get into another players' helmet it's usually a flag," Johnson said. There was no broadcast replay, so here is #Bills Josh Allen’s scrap/fighting against #Dolphins corner Chris Johnson after his first interception via the All-22. #BillsMafia @BuffTrenchTalk pic.twitter.com/5txJ85EpiA — Carson Hayek (@CarsonHayek) November 23, 2026 Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley thought it was a penalty. "I saw it and our guys saw it because they were upset and then they started to talk and I said, I'll handle it," Hafley said. "And then I asked the refs. I'm not going to get into sending it to the league and everything that happened. I just, I don't understand how that is not a penalty. "And that is where I do have a hard time with that. Whatever you want to call happened, to me, that warranted a penalty. And it should have been 15 yards and the ball should have been moved up. So it happened, it's over, it was missed and we'll move on." Allen passed for 304 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in a 26-9 victory. Allen did not have a single rushing attempt. This was likely intentional as the Bills have a game against the Chiefs on Thanksgiving. Allen, apparently, was focused on preserving his energy and health for the Kansas City game. item.title: Senegal re-crowned Afcon champions after appeal upheld
item.description: Senegal have been re-crowned the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations champions after the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) unanimously upheld their appeal against the decision to strip them of their title on Tuesday. Senegal contested Confederation of African Football's (Caf) decision to declare Morocco champions , wiping the Teranga Lions’ title from the records despite winning January’s Afcon final 1-0 after extra time in Rabat. The final was fraught with controversy after Senegal staged a walk-off in protest to a penalty was awarded against them in the dying stages of normal time, with players ordered into the dressing room by manager Pape Thiaw , where they remained for 14 minutes. Play was eventually resumed before Morocco’s Brahim Diaz missed the spot-kick, sailing a tame ‘Panenka’ effort into the arms of Edouard Mendy. Senegal went on to win the match in extra time through Pape Gueye. Brahim Diaz missed the penalty after Senegal staged a 14-minute walk-off (AFP/Getty) However, they were stripped of the title two months later after Caf’s Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited ⁠the match by walking off the pitch, overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 ​victory to ⁠Morocco. Senegal quickly followed with an appeal to sport's highest court, Cas, which was lodged on 25 March and have now successfully fought their case to be reinstated as champions, with the original 1-0 result restored. The three-man Cas ‌panel, presided over by French sports law ​expert Gerald Simon with assistance from ‌Italian international law professor ⁠Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based ⁠attorney Ulrich Haas, ‌unanimously found that referee Jean-Jacques Ndala “did not commit any error of law”, said Cas secretary general Matthieu Reeb. Ndala’s decision to resume the match after Senegal’s walk-off fell within his sole authority and was therefore covered by the “field of play” doctrine, something Morocco’s federation argued was not the case. The court published its reasoning in a press release issued on Tuesday afternoon, which read: “By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met – both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume. “In the panel’s view, there is no doubt that the effects of the referee’s decision were limited to the pitch.” The panel clarified that Articles 82 and 84 of Caf’s tournament regulations, cited in the Moroccan federation’s appeal, apply only to determining match results if team conduct forces a referee to permanently call off a game, and were therefore not applicable in this instance. "In conclusion, the panel considers that in resuming the match, the referee did not err in law," a court press release added. (Photo by FRANCK FIFE / AFP via Getty Images) AFP via Getty Images The Court of Arbitration for Sport finally brought an end on Tuesday to one of the most extraordinary controversies in African soccer , restoring Senegal as champions of the Africa Cup of Nations and overturning a decision that threatened to undermine the authority of the game’s own rules. Nearly a year after that chaotic final in Morocco, Senegal can again celebrate its victory. The CAS ruling is not simply a triumph for the Senegal’s national team. It is also an important affirmation of the principles that should govern the sport: The authority of the match referee, the integrity of the result and the distinction between disciplinary regulations and decisions made during a game. The final was undoubtedly controversial. Senegal defeated Morocco 1-0 after extra time, but the game was overshadowed by a dramatic incident in second-half stoppage time. With the game still scoreless, Morocco was awarded a penalty kick. Senegal’s players protested the decision by leaving the field, resulting in a 15-minute delay. Congolese referee Jean-Jacques Ndala eventually allowed the game to resume. Morocco’s Brahim Diaz subsequently missed the penalty, then Senegal went on to score the decisive goal in extra time and win the game. There was little doubt that Senegal’s walk-off was an unacceptable response to a referee’s decision. Players cannot abandon a match because they disagree with a call. The tournament’s own regulations also provided for a team that refuses to play or leaves the field without the referee’s permission to forfeit the contest. The central question was never whether Senegal’s conduct deserved scrutiny. It was whether the circumstances justified overturning a completed match and later awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory by default. The Confederation of African Football’s appeals panel thought so when it ruled in March that Senegal had forfeited the Jan. 18 final. CAS has now correctly rejected that interpretation. The distinction is crucial. Tournament regulations exist to establish order, protect competition integrity and provide sanctions when teams refuse to fulfill their obligations. But those provisions must be interpreted within the broader framework of the game’s laws and the authority entrusted to referees. item.title: Barca have quality to win without Yamal: De Jong
item.description: Barcelona will be without winger Lamine Yamal for the match at Sabah but Frenkie de Jong says the team have the quality to win without him (Igor IVANKO) Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong backed his team to continue their strong start to the Champions League on Wednesday at Sabah without injured star winger Lamine Yamal. Barca have sometimes struggled without Yamal but De Jong said there was enough quality in the squad to prevail without the Spanish World Cup winner. item.title: UAlbany's Tom Perkovich named finalist for FCS Coach of the Year
item.description: UAlbany new head coach Tom Perkovich during a summer practice on Thursday, July 30, 2026, at Casey Stadium in Albany, NY. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) University at Albany football coach Tom Perkovich, making the jump from Division III, led the Great Danes' turnaround to a Football Championship Subdivision playoff berth in his first season. For that accomplishment, Perkovich was named Tuesday as a finalist for the Eddie Robinson Award, given to the Football Championship Subdivision Coach of the Year, Perkovich is one of 15 finalists for the award, named after the late College Football Hall of Fame coach who guided Grambling for 55 seasons and won 408 games. UAlbany hired Perkovich last December after a successful decade at Division III Susquehanna University to take over a program that went 2-10 last season. The Great Danes were picked 11th in the CAA preseason coaches' poll. Other finalists for this year's award include a pair of former UAlbany assistant coaches, Lamar's Pete Rossomando and Western Illinois' Joe Davis. item.title: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30
item.description: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30 The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings. The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters. Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot. Instead, four fixtures that would ordinarily take place at 19:30 on Sunday evenings would be moved to the new Saturday night slot. The fifth fixture would come from the Friday evening slot on the Easter weekend, with Bundesliga matches not taking place on Good Friday. The proposed changes would coincide with the start of the next domestic broadcasting rights cycle in the summer of 2029.

item.title: Retina Dynamics Brings Robotics to the Breaking Boom
item.description: “There are only so many ways breakers can really differentiate themselves in the market. Operational efficiency is one.” Joseph Owens, former Senior Manager of Live Commerce at Fanatics Live, told me that reality was the driving principle behind his new hardware company, Retina Dynamics. Owens founded the company alongside Matthew Harfmann and Sheridan Skala, with founding engineers Jack Scalise and Eli Thummel leading the technical build. During his tenure at Fanatics, Owens identified back-end logistics as one of the single biggest pain point for breakers, noting that almost every major operator struggled with the tedious, time-consuming process of manually sorting cards after massive product releases . To help alleviate the operations backlog, Retina Dynamics is introducing what it claims is the first automated, robotic sorter built explicitly for breakers and sports card consignment sellers . By introducing a robotic sorting machine to the industry, Owens aims to solve that bottleneck without eliminating jobs . The technology is not designed to replace the human workforce; rather, it allows owners to reallocate those employees away from mundane sorting tasks and into roles that drive better business value, such as customer service, expedited shipping, and social marketing . View this post on Instagram A post shared by Joe (@adhdcollector_joe) The Hardware and Safety Measures The solution is a machine roughly the size of a pinball cabinet . The Retina Dynamics robot uses custom-built, in-house scanning software paired with a specialized “claw” to identify, sort, and organize trading cards . Crucially, the machine is designed to safely handle cards whether they are raw, penny-sleeved, or secured in rigid top-loaders . As a secondary benefit, it captures high-resolution, front-and-back scans of every card as it passes through the system, which can be seamlessly exported for consignment listings . According to Owens, extensive testing went into the physics of the claw to ensure the sorting speed matches human efficiency without risking edge or surface damage to the cards . Pricing and Market Availability The systems are currently being assembled in-house by the company’s full-time engineering team . Production is capped at roughly 15 to 20 units per month to ensure quality control and maintain a manageable 120-day lead time for new buyers . Early demand has already outpaced initial supply: Retina Dynamics has sold out of its initial 20-unit run for November and will reopen for additional pre-orders on December 5. The base unit is priced at $25,000, with an additional $450 monthly subscription required to cover the API data costs associated with reading and identifying the cards . For larger operations requiring three or more machines, the hardware price drops to $22,500 per unit . For more information and to view the sorting machines in action, collectors and breakers can visit retinadynamics.ai .

item.description: The Lakers’ early-season schedule has been a point of contention, but the team’s biggest test of the season is on Friday when Los Angeles takes on the Spurs. San Antonio earned its 15th win of the season Monday, as did the Lakers. The two West rivals boast the best record in the conference, but Spurs color commentator Sean Elliott isn’t convinced by Los Angeles’ strong start to the campaign. Jacob Tobey and Sean Elliott smiles during the game between the Utah Jazz and San Antonio Spurs at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas on October 9, 2024. NBAE via Getty Images “Well, the Lakers aren’t gonna win the NBA championship. They’re not,” Elliott said bluntly on the game broadcast Monday as San Antonio defeated the Kings. “I mean, they’ll be fun to watch. They have really good players. I like Mamu in a Laker uniform . Plus, your best player always, he’s gotta be a stalwart on the defensive end of the floor. I firmly believe that.” Elliott, a former NBA champion with the Spurs in 1999, built a reputation for being a solid two-way player during his career, particularly on the defensive end of the floor. Clearly, he is not a believer that Doncic has made many strides in that area, despite what many people say. He went on to list the Spurs, Thunder, Knicks and 76ers as potential championship teams . In spite of the mass amount of injuries for Oklahoma City, the former NBA champion believes they have a better chance at this year’s title than the Lakers do. Luka Doncic #77 of the Los Angeles Lakers looks on during the game against the Utah Jazz on November 23, 2026 at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles, California. NBAE via Getty Images San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama walks up court between plays in the second half of an NBA basketball game against the New Orleans Pelicans, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in San Antonio. AP Photo/Darren Abate The heavy usage of Luka Doncic has also been a sticking point for skeptics. Doncic is central to helping the Lakers make a deep playoff run, but many argue his workload is unsustainable throughout the regular season and beyond. Earlier on the broadcast, Elliott praised Doncic for his otherworldly performance this season, but noted that his usage rate quickly puts the purple and gold out of championship contention. He is averaging just over 36 minutes per game. But that is nothing new for the Slovenian sharpshooter. Doncic has averaged between 32 and 37 minutes every season of his nine-year career. Nevertheless, Friday’s game should be a fair litmus test for the Lakers and their skeptics.

item.title: Denny Hamlin Sets Hard Line On NASCAR Retirement Plans
item.description: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Denny Hamlin has made his stance clear to the NASCAR world . The 46-year-old driver plans to end his full-time Cup Series career after the 2027 season. He will not stick around just to fill a seat if his skills fade. This decision comes despite strong pressure from team owner Joe Gibbs to reconsider the timeline. Hamlin told SiriusXM NASCAR Radio that his final call depends entirely on his ability to win races every weekend. Joe Gibbs has been trying to change Hamlin’s mind for some time. The team owner visits the driver’s home in the evenings to discuss the future. Hamlin described these late-night talks on the couch as a normal part of their relationship. “Joe does his normal thing. He just pops in at the house at 8-9 p.m. at night and sits on the couch and has a discussion with you. That’s already started,” Hamlin said, according to MotorBiscuit . The conversations have begun, but the driver’s mind seems set on a specific path. Winning Is the Only Option Hamlin refuses to drive a car he cannot win with. He knows that staying in the sport without a chance at victory would feel wrong. The driver explained that his competitive fire is what keeps him behind the wheel. “If I know that I’m not going to be able to win every single weekend, there’s just no way I can do it,” Hamlin said. This standard is non-negotiable for a driver with his track record. He finished third in the Cup Series standings last year and won four races. The driver also wants to protect the legacy of Joe Gibbs Racing. He plans to ensure the team has a new driver ready before he steps away. Hamlin does not want to leave the organization in a bind or hold back their progress. “I want to make sure they’ve got their next driver planned, lined up — all that stuff. I’m definitely going to do whatever is best for Joe Gibbs Racing, but I’m not going to compromise my performance,” Hamlin said. He values the team but will not sacrifice his own speed to help them. The Clock Is Ticking Hamlin admits that his body feels the toll of racing more than it used to. He senses that his physical edge is slipping away slowly. This feeling in daily life is a warning sign for his time on the track. “I can feel it. In my everyday life, I can tell things are changing. It’s a matter of time before it changes on the racetrack. It just is. I want to avoid that at all costs,” Hamlin said. He wants to leave while he is still at the top of his game. Hamlin is not making this choice based on money or contract terms. He noted that Gibbs has been fair with him throughout his 21-year career. The decision is purely about pride and the desire to compete at the highest level. He feels content with the idea of hanging up his helmet after two more years. Hamlin also said he wants to talk to retired drivers like Kevin Harvick to learn from their experiences.

item.title: Why Packers’ Offensive Line Could Look Different After Bye
item.description: Green Bay Packers head coach Matt LaFleur. Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Getty The Green Bay Packers offensive line has had anything but continuity through the 2026 season. While head coach Matt LaFleur admitted that this has been a major issue for the team, he also acknowledged that there is a chance for them to find continuity between their bye week and the end of the season. “I think continuity is critical,” said LaFleur when discussing offensive line continuity. “Especially when you’re talking about the offensive line, where you need five guys working as one. So I think that is a huge component in terms of your ability to go out there and have consistent success.” The Packers coach added that experience is also important. “I also think just, you know, the experience of that group up front plays a pivotal role in that as well,” added LaFleur. The Packers have only had Jordan Morgan at left tackle start every game at the same position. They have had multiple starters at the four other spots. Green Bay Packers Hoping to Find Offensive Line Continuity Getty (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) Now, the team has a chance to find some continuity. Jordan Morgan is still at left tackle and Anthony Belton has been starting at right tackle since Week 3. They are high on Laken Tomlinson at left guard, and if Kevin Zeitler and Sean Rhyan are healthy, they are going to start at right guard and center, respectively. As long as there are not any injuries this unit is going to be what leads the team into a playoff push. While LaFleur is excited to see the continuity, his message to the unit is to handle what they have to. “You know, my thing is this: it really— at the end of the day, it doesn’t matter,” said LaFleur. “You got a job to go, and you got to go perform well. And if you don’t, then it’s going to get scrutinized, and it is what it is. But it’s never an excuse. You still— that’s why you prepare everybody.” Packers Not Making Excuses LaFleur noted that he thinks that everyone on the roster needs to be ready to be called into duty. “I mean, whether you’re on the active or you’re a P-squad guy, you got to be ready to play, and you got to be ready to do your part. So it’s just— it’s the circumstance that every team in the league faces.” It almost comes off as if LaFleur realized in his first answer that he was making an excuse of not having continuity and then tried to defend it by saying that the depth has to be ready. item.title: Preview: Eintracht travel to Stuttgart
item.description: Preview: Eintracht travel to Stuttgart Boosted by their victory over Hoffenheim, the Eagles take on direct rivals VfB Stuttgart away from home on Saturday evening – a fixture which is almost guaranteed to produce goals. Looking to build consistency Following Saturday’s 1-0 home win over TSG Hoffenheim, Adi Hütter’s Eintracht Frankfurt side have picked up seven points from their last three Bundesliga assignments, lifting them into seventh place in the standings. “We have a young team that wants to become even more consistent, and these are exactly the types of games that help us build confidence and gain experience,” said Eagles sporting director Timmo Hardung. “We want to build on that in Stuttgart.” Opponents VfB, who drew 0-0 at promoted FC Schalke 04 last time out, are currently two points behind Eintracht in eighth spot. “We know it won’t be an easy game but if we build on our recent performances, battle together and stay compact, we have a good chance of picking up another three points,” said Oscar Højlund. Steeped in tradition Saturday evening’s primetime fixture (kick-off 18:30 CET) is one with a lot of history. The two teams are facing each other for the 107th time in the Bundesliga on Matchday 11, with Stuttgart boasting 45 wins to Eintracht’s 37. The sides have shared the spoils on 24 occasions, including in their most recent meeting on Matchday 34 last term, when they played out a 2-2 draw. Goals guaranteed There has not been a goalless draw between the Eagles and VfB since 26 May 1994, when goalkeepers Uli Stein and Eike Immel both kept clean sheets in the City Forest. Remarkably, 61 years have passed since the last stalemate between the sides in Stuttgart. Peter Kunter was in goal for Eintracht that day, with the likes of Friedel Lutz, Dieter Lindner and Jürgen Grabowski also featuring in the game on 18 September 1965. This weekend, Hütter’s charges will be perfectly happy with a repeat of the narrow win they secured against Hoffenheim last time out. “That gives us momentum and confidence,” said Elias Baum. “We’re in great spirits. In the next few games, we’ll try to keep it going. Hopefully, at the end of the year, we’ll be in a position that enables us to keep looking up the table.” The Eagles have four more league games before Christmas, as well as a DFB-Pokal last-16 tie against Borussia Dortmund. For now, though, their focus is firmly on Stuttgart this Saturday.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. But it’s not.” Nor is it up to the team’s most loyal supporters, who would like to see someone sacrificed for the team’s fall from grace. item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville.
